description: A battalion executive officer must publish the schedule for a one-day sustainment skills validation, placing four training modules into four available blocks and recording the coordination control for each module.

shared_context.S1: The sustainment skills validation has four modules: vehicle recovery procedures, load-planning procedures, radio-setup procedures, and heat-injury response.
shared_context.S2: The available training blocks are 0800-1000, 1000-1200, 1300-1500, and 1500-1700, with one module scheduled in each block.
shared_context.S3: Maj. Alvarez publishes the final schedule, and each module requires a written coordination control before the schedule is released.
shared_context.S4: The normal pre-publication staff huddle includes the S-3, maintenance control, signal, and medical readiness officers reporting changes to their training requirements.

PF1.text: A higher-headquarters evaluator will observe the load-planning procedures module at exactly 1500 on validation day; Capt. Morgan received the evaluator's visit notice this morning, but the observation time is not yet on the battalion training slide.

PF2.text: The certified recovery rig needed for the vehicle recovery procedures module is booked for a safety inspection from 0800 through 1200, so that module can begin only in the 1300-1500 block; SFC Patel confirmed the booking with the motor pool this morning, but the maintenance calendar has not been attached to the training packet.

PF3.text: The radio-setup procedures module must use the signal shelter after its frequency load is completed at 0930, making the 1000-1200 block the first usable block; Lt. Brooks received the programming work order from the signal shop this morning, but the completion time is not on the training schedule.

PF4.text: The only instructor certified to evaluate the heat-injury response module is available at exactly 0800-1000 and is assigned to another duty after 1000; Lt. Okafor confirmed the duty roster today, but the instructor assignment has not been entered in the validation roster.

acceptance_conditions: Heat-injury response must be scheduled for 0800-1000.
Radio-setup procedures must be scheduled for 1000-1200.
Vehicle recovery procedures must be scheduled for 1300-1500.
Load-planning procedures must be scheduled for 1500-1700.
A control commitment must record the higher-headquarters observation for the load-planning module.
A control commitment must record the recovery-rig inspection constraint.
A control commitment must record signal-shelter readiness for the radio module.
A control commitment must record the certified medical instructor assignment.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'higher_headquarters_observation' and c['target'] == 'load_planning' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'recovery_rig_inspection_control' and c['target'] == 'vehicle_recovery' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'signal_shelter_readiness' and c['target'] == 'radio_setup' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'certified_medical_instructor_assignment' and c['target'] == 'heat_response' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The evaluator's exact 1500 observation changes load-planning from an unspecific placement to the 1500-1700 block and requires the observation control.
The recovery rig's 0800-1200 inspection changes vehicle recovery to the 1300-1500 block and requires an inspection control.
The 0930 frequency-load completion changes radio setup to the first usable 1000-1200 block and requires signal-shelter readiness.
The certified instructor's 0800-1000 availability changes heat response to that exact block and requires a medical-instructor assignment.
